/-!
# Erdős Problem 1094

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1094](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1094)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1094

open scoped Nat

/--
For all $n\ge 2k$ the least prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$ is $\le\max(n/k,k)$, with only
finitely many exceptions.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1094 :
    {(n, k) : ℕ × ℕ | 0 < k ∧ 2 * k ≤ n ∧ (n.choose k).minFac > max (n / k) k}.Finite := by
  sorry

end Erdos1094

reformulations.difference: Lean uses natural-number division in max (n / k) k, whereas the published upper bound uses the ordinary quotient. It also expresses finitely many exceptions as finiteness of the set of violating pairs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For natural numbers n, k, p with k > 0, max (n / k) k < p is equivalent to n < p*k ∧ k < p. The real-valued inequality max ((n : ℝ) / k) k < p is equivalent to exactly the same conditions. Thus the exceptional sets coincide. Their finiteness is equivalent to the real-valued upper bound holding for all but finitely many admissible pairs. Both equivalences were proved in the scratch file, independently of the conjecture.

review.notes: No mathematical defect was identified. Lean proofs confirm that 0 < k and 2*k ≤ n exclude binomial coefficients 0 and 1, so Nat.minFac's exceptional conventions are unreachable. The k = 1 case satisfies the bound. Computations checked boundary cases and all admissible pairs with n ≤ 100. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully; the equivalence proofs do not depend on sorryAx. The 1988 paper gives the same domain and upper bound in a stronger conjecture specifying 14 exceptions. The current community database records problem 1094 as open, consistent with the file's category. Direct verification against the cited webpage remains limited as described below.
